extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of Charles Lamb; literary critics and teachers; users/distributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: Appreciation and use of Charles Lamb's letters (Elia) including how to read and criticize them, plus the practical/licensing rules for redistributing the Project Gutenberg eBook. Useful for readers, teachers, editors, and distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naïve enjoyment as a critical method
rubrics_metrics.description: Charles Lamb's critical value is grounded in a capacity of 'naïve enjoyment' — enjoying the savor of a book without pragmatically analyzing or explaining every quaint passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-refining and analytic prying; relish books for their obvious beauties rather than trying to resolve every image into a riddle. The essayist's power lies in discerning beauty and making readers discern it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-analysis and speculative parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hunt for riddles in metaphors, innuendoes in tropes, or ciphers in great authors; excessive exposition and 'explaining' can ruin enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should not 'resolve' literature into ingenious rebuses or pry apart pleasures into mechanistic explanations; favor appreciation over exhaustive dissection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach appreciation rather than parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Schoolmasters and teachers should encourage ingenuous appreciation of poetry and prose rather than parsing and grammatical dissection that breeds detestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For learners, permit 'unlearnedly' sitting at the feet of writers (like Keats with Chapman) rather than forcing classical parsing that kills enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of Elia-style essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Elia (Lamb's persona) is characterized by being 'wise, playful, tender, fantastic' and by a style 'everything by starts, and nothing long.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or attempting Elia-like prose, look for felicitous phrase, intermittent impulses rather than sustained arguments, playfulness blended with tenderness and fantasy, and an economy that favors brief, vivid sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discerning and transmitting beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong critic/essayist discerns beauty in a work and adds to readers' enjoyment by making them discern it as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of prose should account for the writer's power to increase communal pleasure in literature, not merely technical correctness or exhaustive interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution with epithets and sentimental labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid careless, conventional epithets (e.g., calling Lamb 'gentle-hearted') without considering the equivocal nature and possible mischaracterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise and considerate when labeling authors or works; consider how epithets may distort perception of character or style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical context as interpretive aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Lamb's life events (family history, education, illness, employment, friendships) are presented as important context for understanding his letters and essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or teaching Lamb's letters, incorporate relevant biographical details (e.g., Christ's Hospital, East India Company service, sister Mary's illness) to illuminate themes and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of modest publication and revival of neglected authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Lamb's work (e.g., Specimens of the English Dramatic Poets) is credited with reviving interest in neglected Elizabethan dramatists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments of a writer's importance may include their influence on literary taste and canon-formation, not only immediate commercial success.
